timeline.event: Electron-beam irradiation of polyacrylonitrile precursor fibers was shown to shorten the thermal stabilization step by about one quarter.
A review of lignin-based carbon fibers measured progress against a US Department of Energy target of 1.72 GPa strength and 172 GPa modulus, which few studies had approached.
A factory study in Japan found carbon fiber fragments meeting the WHO respirable fiber definition during cutting and grinding of carbon fiber reinforced plastics.
Pyrolysis followed by oxidation was reported as a route for recovering carbon fibers from waste composites.

timeline.event: IARC evaluated man-made mineral fibres for carcinogenic hazard.

IARC re-evaluated man-made vitreous fibres: insulation glass wool moved from Group 2B to Group 3 and continuous glass filament was placed in Group 3, while special-purpose glass fibres stayed in Group 2B.
Flame-barrier layers in two mattress covers were found to contain over 50% fiberglass, with up to about 1% migrating to adjacent layers.

A pilot-plant pyrolysis study recovered glass fibers from composites that did not meet the WHO respirable fiber definition, though residual coatings carried traces of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

timeline.event: French engineer Paul Dhe proposed manufacturing fiber from basalt, but no production followed.
The Soviet Union first extracted basalt fiber.
Industrial basalt fiber production began in Ukraine, initially for defense uses and with high energy consumption.
A new-generation process cut energy use by about 2.5 times.
A continuous tank-kiln basalt fiber line with an annual capacity of 8,000 tons began operating in Deyang, Sichuan, in March.

production.scope: basalt fiber output in China only (no verified world total)

timeline.event: Gilt silver threads were made by gilding silver and joining the gold by diffusion bonding; focused ion beam cross-sections detected no mercury.
In Croatian collections, threads shifted from gilded silver on silk toward cheaper silver, copper and alloy threads, with copper on cotton cores predominating in more recent pieces.
Laundering tests found that all silver-treated textiles studied, conventional or nano-silver, released silver particles into wash water.
A silane-bonded silver-plated cellulose fabric stayed below 2 ohm/sq and about 92.82% antibacterial after 200 washes, in a study of wearable electrodes.

properties.conditions: refractory ceramic fiber after long service at or above this temperature

timeline.event: Rodent inhalation studies reported fibrosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma after refractory ceramic fiber exposure, though high doses complicate interpretation.
A review summarized workplace monitoring of refractory ceramic fiber exposure in the United States.
IARC classified refractory ceramic fibres as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B) in its re-evaluation of man-made vitreous fibres.
NIOSH published criteria for a recommended standard, with a recommended exposure limit of 0.5 fibers per cubic centimeter as a 10-hour time-weighted average.
Alkaline earth silicate wools were reviewed as a biosoluble replacement for refractory ceramic fiber in high-temperature insulation.
A 30-year study of US refractory ceramic fiber workers reported pleural changes in 6.1% overall and 21.4% in the highest cumulative exposure group, with no increase in lung cancer mortality.
